name: PyHSS
what_it_is: PyHSS is a Python 3 Home Subscriber Server (HSS) and subscriber data management solution for LTE (4G) Evolved Packet Core networks. It implements multiple 3GPP network functions—HSS, VoLTE HSS, EIR, PCRF, BSF, and GMLC—via Diameter and GSUP interfaces, backed by a REST API for subscriber CRUD operations.
components: diameterService — Diameter protocol listener and peer connection manager (TCP or SCTP, port 3868)
hssService — Diameter request encoder/decoder and HSS business logic processor
apiService — Swagger-documented RESTful API for subscriber data management (port 8080)
georedService — Geographic redundancy coordinator and webhook handler
logService — Centralised logging aggregator for all microservices
gsupService — GSUP interface handler for OpenBSC/Osmocom peers (port 4222)
protocols: Diameter S6a — MME/HSS authentication and location management
Diameter S13 — Equipment Identity Register (EIR) device verification
Diameter Cx — P-CSCF/S-CSCF authentication and routing for IMS/VoLTE
Diameter SLh — Subscriber location discovery for GMLC
Diameter Sh — Application Server access to HSS subscriber data
Diameter Zh/Zn — GBA credential generation (BSF role)
Diameter Gx — Credit control and PCRF charging rules
GSUP — Osmocom Generic Subscriber Update Protocol for 2G/3G core interop
measurement: SNMP support retained for legacy backward compatibility
Tested subscriber capacity: over 1 million subscribers
configuration: config.yaml — single file for all runtime parameters
hss.MCC / hss.MNC — Home PLMN for subscriber context
hss.client_socket_timeout — idle Diameter peer disconnect timer (seconds)
hss.diameter_request_timeout — max wait before discarding a Diameter request (default 3 s)
hss.lock_provisioning / hss.provisioning_key — API key guard for subscriber writes
hss.CancelLocationRequest_Enabled — send CLR to old MME on new MME attach
hss.use_dra_fallback — route via DRA when target peer is unreachable
hss.emergency_subscriber_expiry — TTL in minutes for emergency subscriber entries
hss.scscf_pool — list of S-CSCF FQDNs for IMS routing
Docker .env file — overrides config.yaml values per container role via CONTAINER_ROLE env var
Database backend selectable: MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQLite
modes: HSS — standard LTE subscriber authentication and location management
VoLTE HSS — IMS/VoLTE subscriber profile management via Cx/Sh interfaces
EIR (Equipment Identity Register) — device IMEI verification via S13
PCRF — policy and charging rules function via Gx interface
BSF (Bootstrapping Server Function) — GBA credential generation via Zh/Zn
GMLC (Gateway Mobile Location Centre) — subscriber location via SLh
Trusting Diameter mode — accepts connections from any peer without peer verification
constraints: Requires Redis 7.0.0+ as a mandatory external dependency for inter-service message queuing
SCTP transport is marked experimental; only TCP has been load-tested for production
Diameter operates in trusting mode by default — no peer certificate or shared-secret authentication
No TLS/DTLS encryption mentioned for Diameter connections
No built-in rate limiting or DDoS protection for Diameter or API endpoints
docker-compose binds all ports to 127.0.0.1 only — external Diameter peers cannot connect without network reconfiguration

docker_services.name: pyhss_api
docker_services.role: REST API server for subscriber CRUD and OAM

docker_services.name: pyhss_diameter
docker_services.role: Diameter protocol listener and peer connection manager

docker_services.name: pyhss_hss
docker_services.role: HSS business logic processor (Diameter request handler)

docker_services.name: pyhss_gsup
docker_services.role: GSUP interface handler for Osmocom/OpenBSC 2G/3G peers

docker_services.name: redis
docker_services.role: Inter-service message queue and active peer state store

notable_absences: No fault injection or chaos testing hooks present
No TLS/DTLS support for Diameter transport encryption
No Diameter peer authentication (shared secrets or certificates)
No georedService or metricService containers in docker-compose (run outside compose or not containerised)
No multi-region or cross-datacenter deployment guidance beyond clustering mention
No backup or disaster recovery procedures documented
